parameter: basis for human applicability of rat RPFs - persistence parallelism argument
value: RPF similar to or higher than PFOA
model: read-across on the assumption that rat-human kinetic rank order is preserved
primary_source_cited: RIVM Annex II Table A2
assumptions: 'This coincides with the even more persistent behaviour of these congeners in the rat when compared with PFOA. Because such kinetic characteristics are paralleled in man, it has been concluded that, as a first tier, the derived RPFs of these compounds hold for humans as well.' RIVM assumes rank-order conservation of half-life between rat and human without quantitative demonstration.
standard_type: Relative Potency Factors and Health-Based Guidance Value (used for drinking water and soil risk limits)

agency: RIVM (Netherlands National Institute for Public Health and the Environment)
document: Mixture exposure to PFAS: a Relative Potency Factor approach (RIVM Report 2018-0070)
parameter: exception to the persistence argument - ABSORPTION rather than elimination governs
value: low RPF despite expected high persistence
model: absorption-limited read-across
primary_source_cited: RIVM BMD analysis (Annex IV)
assumptions: 'By analogy, a quite persistent behaviour, with correspondingly high RPF, is expected for PFHxDA and PFODA. However, the contrary was found to be the case, most probably due to the negligible absorption of these two congeners. Again, this is expected to hold for humans too.' The only place in this survey where an agency identifies ABSORPTION, not elimination, as the controlling kinetic step for the longest-chain PFAS.
standard_type: Relative Potency Factors and Health-Based Guidance Value (used for drinking water and soil risk limits)

document: Mixture exposure to PFAS: a Relative Potency Factor approach (RIVM Report 2018-0070)
